title: Twenty First Word First Station Fifth Warning Rejecting Worldly Busyness As An Excuse

questions.question: What main excuse for neglecting worship is challenged at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The excuse that a person is too busy with worldly work and daily responsibilities to make time for prayer.

questions.question: According to the passage, what comparison is made between human beings and animals in earning a living?
questions.answer: Humans may have higher abilities overall, but in getting basic worldly needs they are not better than even small animals, so their main purpose cannot be just survival.

questions.question: What is presented as the real duty of a human being?
questions.answer: To work for an enduring life beyond this temporary world and live with a truly human purpose.

questions.question: How does the passage describe many things people call worldly business?
questions.answer: It says many of them are not truly necessary and are matters people involve themselves in without real need.

questions.question: What examples are given to show how people waste valuable time?
questions.answer: Spending time on remote facts and minor information, like details about Saturn’s rings or counting chickens in America.

questions.question: What point is made by those examples?
questions.answer: People often act as if they will remain in this world for an extremely long time, so they chase low-priority knowledge and neglect what matters most.

questions.question: In the example about wages and digging, what is the person being offered?
questions.answer: A brief task that would lead to a treasure far more valuable than the small amount of pay he fears losing.

questions.question: Why is refusing that offer called foolish?
questions.answer: Because the small loss is nothing compared with the enormous gain that could be received in return.

questions.question: How is that example connected to the obligatory prayers?
questions.answer: Leaving prayer for the sake of worldly work is like refusing huge profit in order to avoid a tiny loss.

questions.question: What are the two benefits found by using rest times for prayer?
questions.answer: Prayer supports both a blessed worldly livelihood and provision for the life to come.

questions.question: What question is asked to challenge the idea that worldly busyness excuses laziness in worship?
questions.answer: Whether a person was created only for this world so that all of life should be spent on worldly concerns.

questions.question: Why does the passage say this worldly-only mindset is beneath a human being?
questions.answer: Because a human being has a higher purpose than merely chasing food and survival like animals do.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about many activities that fill people’s schedules?
questions.answer: Many are side issues that do not truly belong to their core responsibilities.

questions.question: How does the passage describe a person who spends time on trivial facts while neglecting worship?
questions.answer: As someone acting as though he expects to stay in this world for a very long time.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the example involving Saturn and chickens?
questions.answer: To show that people may devote energy to useless information while ignoring what benefits their souls.

questions.question: In the wage example, what does the small wage represent?
questions.answer: The limited worldly return a person chases in everyday work.

questions.question: In that same example, what do the valuable jewels represent?
questions.answer: The great rewards and deeper gains connected with fulfilling prayer and worship.

questions.question: What does the orchard symbolize in the passage?
questions.answer: The place where a person works for provision in this worldly life.

questions.question: What happens if someone keeps working for livelihood but leaves the obligatory prayers?
questions.answer: The results of that labor stay narrow, worldly, and lacking lasting fruit.

questions.question: Why are rest periods especially mentioned as times for prayer?
questions.answer: Because prayer in those times refreshes the spirit and heart without blocking a person from earning a living.

questions.question: What false assumption about time is criticized in the opening of the passage?
questions.answer: The assumption that worldly duties are so overwhelming that they leave no room for worship.

questions.question: What reason is given for saying that this excuse is not valid?
questions.answer: Because human beings were not made only for temporary worldly survival.

questions.question: How does the passage use animals to put human life in perspective?
questions.answer: It points out that even animals can secure worldly needs effectively, so human excellence must lie in a higher purpose.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should a true human being seek?
questions.answer: A lasting life and meaningful effort directed toward what continues beyond death.

questions.question: What criticism is made of people’s involvement in so-called worldly occupations?
questions.answer: They often interfere in matters that are minor and not truly central to their responsibilities.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about learning trivial facts while neglecting prayer?
questions.answer: It shows misplaced priorities and poor judgment about what deserves one’s time.

questions.question: In the illustration about lost wages, what kind of reasoning is being exposed?
questions.answer: Short-sighted thinking that clings to a tiny immediate benefit while overlooking a much greater return.

questions.question: Why is the comparison with treasure effective in explaining prayer?
questions.answer: Because it makes clear that a small worldly sacrifice can open the way to immense gain.

questions.question: What two kinds of provision are connected to prayer in the orchard example?
questions.answer: Support in this world and lasting provision in the hereafter.

questions.question: How does prayer affect the spirit and heart according to that example?
questions.answer: It gives the spirit calm and allows the heart relief and renewal.

questions.question: What kind of self is being addressed in this warning?
questions.answer: A self absorbed in worldly life and therefore careless about worship.

questions.question: What two possible reasons for neglecting prayer are mentioned first?
questions.answer: Being overwhelmed by worldly tasks and claiming there is no time because of earning a living.

questions.question: What larger question is used to challenge both excuses?
questions.answer: Whether a person’s creation was meant only for this temporary world.

questions.question: What contrast does the passage make between human capacity and a sparrow?
questions.answer: Even with greater human abilities, a person is not better than a sparrow at simply obtaining worldly necessities.

questions.question: What lesson should be drawn from that contrast?
questions.answer: That human life must have a higher mission than just material striving.

questions.question: How does the passage judge much of what people call worldly occupation?
questions.answer: As unnecessary involvement in minor matters rather than truly urgent responsibilities.

questions.question: What does wasting time on distant facts reveal about a person’s mindset?
questions.answer: It reveals that he is living as if this world were permanent for him.

questions.question: In the labor-and-jewels example, what does the ten-minute task stand for?
questions.answer: The brief effort required for prayer.

questions.question: What does the fear of losing part of the daily wage stand for?
questions.answer: The worry that prayer will reduce worldly earnings or productivity.

questions.question: According to the passage, why is that fear unreasonable?
questions.answer: Because the gain from prayer is immensely greater than any small worldly loss a person imagines.

questions.question: What does the passage say prayer adds for the hereafter?
questions.answer: It provides lasting sustenance and provisions beyond this world.

questions.question: What final outcome is described for someone who leaves prayer?
questions.answer: He loses great spiritual profit, grows tired of his work, and drifts toward hopeless laziness.

questions.question: What problem in worship is the passage mainly addressing?
questions.answer: Becoming careless and weak in performing the required prayers because of attachment to worldly concerns.

questions.question: How does the passage challenge the claim that livelihood leaves no time for worship?
questions.answer: It argues that earning a living is not the whole purpose of human existence.

questions.question: Why is the human being said to be greater than animals in one sense but not in another?
questions.answer: Humans have broader abilities and a higher calling, yet they are not superior to animals in the basic act of securing material needs.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from that comparison?
questions.answer: A human being’s primary task must be something nobler than material struggle alone.

questions.question: What mistake does the passage say people make with many worldly matters?
questions.answer: They treat side issues as if they were major responsibilities.

questions.question: Why are examples of obscure information included in the passage?
questions.answer: To expose how people can pour effort into low-value knowledge while neglecting what benefits them most.

questions.question: In the example of the worker, what does the offered treasure teach about religious duties?
questions.answer: That a small investment of time in worship can bring reward far beyond ordinary worldly earnings.

questions.question: What kind of excuse is being criticized through that example?
questions.answer: The excuse that prayer costs too much time or income.

questions.question: What happens to one’s labor if obligatory prayer is abandoned?
questions.answer: Its outcome remains limited to a narrow, low-level worldly gain.

questions.question: What special role do prayer times play during a person’s day of work?
questions.answer: They provide renewal for the inner life while also opening the way to greater blessing in both worlds.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the person who keeps both worship and lawful work together?
questions.answer: As someone energized by faith and eager to prepare for the grave and the next life.

questions.question: What sort of attitude toward the world is criticized in this warning?
questions.answer: A mindset that gives worldly life too much importance and lets worship become secondary.

questions.question: What practical question about prayer is raised at the start?
questions.answer: Whether a person’s delay and carelessness in prayer come from busyness and the demands of making a living.

questions.question: What answer does the passage give to the idea that worldly work is our whole purpose?
questions.answer: It rejects that idea and says humans are meant for more than temporary worldly labor.

questions.question: What role does the image of the sparrow play in the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that pure material survival is not the field in which human worth is highest.

questions.question: What is the passage teaching when it says one should live like a true human being?
questions.answer: One should aim for an everlasting life and live according to a higher spiritual mission.

questions.question: How does the passage expose false busyness?
questions.answer: By showing that much of what fills people’s time is minor, unnecessary, and self-imposed.

questions.question: What does pretending to need endless information about remote topics reveal?
questions.answer: It reveals attachment to trivial matters and forgetfulness of life’s real priorities.

questions.question: In the example of the daily worker, what does the cut in wages represent?
questions.answer: The small worldly cost a person fears when taking time for prayer.

questions.question: What do the precious stones represent in that same example?
questions.answer: The immense value and reward hidden in worship.

questions.question: What lesson is drawn from comparing prayer to that profitable offer?
questions.answer: Neglecting prayer to protect worldly earnings is irrational because the trade is overwhelmingly in one’s favor.

questions.question: What are the two broad outcomes of praying during one’s breaks from work?
questions.answer: The person gains support for a better worldly livelihood and also stores provision for the afterlife.
